LogEx query execution ownership correction

Complete published datafusion-physical-plan 51.0.0 package, Apache License 2.0.
Original license, notice, package files and tests are retained. No version upgrade.
Archive SHA-256: 0acf0ad6b6924c6b1aa7d213b181e012e2d3ec0a64ff5b10ee6282ab0f8532ac
Published VCS commit: fd35a09438a2b4841431f5e86ffef378cbbda7c9
Original inventory: LOGEX-UPSTREAM-SHA256
Complete source correction and regression: LOGEX-PATCH.diff

The parallel in-memory sort path creates internal streams, then sends their
results from background tasks. Its one-shot sort future releases its memory
reservation before yielding. Neither that completed future nor its buffering
task necessarily retains TaskContext or RuntimeEnv. Aborting an outer stream
also does not synchronously stop a task that is executing CPU work.

Retain Arc<RuntimeEnv> in an outer map on each internal stream, until the
buffering task releases that stream. LogEx's per-query forwarding memory pool
owns the admission lease through this RuntimeEnv; execution-plan child streams
own it separately. Sort algorithms, buffering, parallelism and reservation sizes
are unchanged. This corrects ownership, not query-memory limits. LogEx disables
query disk spill; spill-reader ownership is outside this correction's scope.

The bounded regression forces two tiny batches into the actual internal-sort
branch on a current-thread runtime, drops external runtime owners, consumes an
output batch, and checks retention then release. It requires no scheduler race,
network, production data or wall-clock performance assumption. Workspace tests
cover plan/cancellation ownership and recursive/result semantics. Excluded vendor
tests run separately on both CI platforms:

CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/physical-plan-regressions cargo test --manifest-path vendor/datafusion-physical-plan/Cargo.toml --lib logex_internal --locked

Verify complete source and reviewed differences with:
python3 tools/verify_datafusion_vendor.py

Remove this override only when a maintained engine provides equivalent internal
stream/task ownership and passes LogEx query compatibility and lifetime tests.
